title: Implement the accepted capability and lawful-runtime synthesis

labels.name: wayfinder:task
labels.description: Execution authorized in the Effra Wayfinder map

repository.name: effra
repository.description: An experimental server language with explicit effect contracts, owned lifetimes, native Go executables and a JavaScript/Effect target.

body:
<!-- effra-wayfinder-id: capability-synthesis -->
<!-- effra-wayfinder-source-sha256: 54e8f1f03b533f16f81be718eeced40bf00c583fd05c88784e2a97749f5abf0c -->
<!-- effra-wayfinder-source-commit: 4627f414414cc964840b53894b7161482687de69 -->

Turn the accepted synthesis design into finite, independently gated repository units. The design is a source-backed decision artifact only; it does not implement externs, resource types, receiver methods, equality, host laws or runtime substitution.

## Acceptance

- Implement bundled-only extern scope/catalog facts, target-qualified host bindings and explicit ABI/failure/service rows. User extern escape, ambient capability admission and invalid target bindings diagnose.
- Implement constructor-less `extern [resource] type` and owner-controlled `pub readonly` data construction/ingress with nominal identity, ownership and equality/hash controls. Resource handles have no Effra constructors or structural codec shortcut.
- Implement ordinary receiver methods, pipe and constant-only defaults only where their checked prerequisites hold. Resolution is receiver-owned, source order and public rows remain visible, and no overload/extension/implicit witness search is introduced.
- Define and execute the finite lawful-runtime evidence suite in the lawful runtime contract (public source sync pending: `docs/research/lawful-runtime-contract.md`): RS1 is the P1–P12/R1–R15 cross-target partial-order suite with its R1/R4/R7/R11 gaps and m1–m3 controls; RS2 separately makes P9 managed wait public, keeps latch/layers on the public core and checks for private-core references. Distinguish nominally checked, trusted decision, tested law, refuted and unresolved/unavailable evidence; preserve cancellation classification, defects, cleanup causes and completed shutdown.
- Implement provider selection only for a scoped, reviewed lawful effect/runtime contract. Pinned Effect remains the default/reference provider and the current JS ABI remains Effect-compatible; an alternate userland provider must declare its actual representation, ABI, effect/service/failure/ownership rows, cancellation and cleanup behavior, and machine interoperation rather than pretending a different representation is the default. Exercise two same-target unrelated provider callers where that contract is selected, plus negative controls for implicit execution, row mismatch and incomplete cleanup. A visible runtime selection remains deferred until a second real provider exists.
- Keep public contracts, inspection, source revisions and provider selection coherent across Go/JS. No hidden `any`, erased `R`, private runtime hook or benchmark-specific facade. Each unit needs causal negative controls, full gate and independent frozen review.

Synthesis remains implementation work after the accepted design review. It does not close any HITL ticket or establish a production release by prose.

Define and implement client-profile lifetime semantics through a user-selected pragma and lawful runtime/provider boundary, with React, Solid 2 and solid-yield as host validation targets. The lawful runtime contract (public source sync pending: `docs/research/lawful-runtime-contract.md`) supplies the shared law-obligation categories and completed-shutdown evidence boundary. A provider may distinguish inert server markup from a client element with deferred code, retained state and host callbacks under a mount lifetime, but the compiler does not mandate `View.Node`/`Client.Element` names or a bespoke framework adapter API. JSX notation and a source gallery do not establish this bridge.

## Acceptance

- Keep the selected provider's server/client representations distinct in types, profiles and inspection. A client constructor/runtime owns mount, update, error and disposal lifetimes; callbacks and subscriptions cannot escape that owner.
- Preserve Effra rows and cancellation through the selected host runtime with explicit Pending/Failed/Ready or equivalent state, stale-response fencing, disconnect/unmount cleanup and error-boundary behavior. Preserve declared services and failures through the bridge; no unchecked `any`, hidden provider or compiler-hardcoded framework adapter.
- Exercise one React, one Solid 2 and one pinned solid-yield fixture with actual mount/update/dispose behavior through the selected pragma/runtime boundary, plus negative controls for retained callbacks, unresolved requirements and late responses. Record framework/runtime versions and source hashes.
- Keep hydration, streaming, SSR parity and external transactional guarantees separate. Full gate and independent review are required before a framework row becomes verified.

This is VW4 acceptance work; the current gallery and source sketches remain reference/design evidence.

title: One-to-one JSX view notation (VW6)

labels.name: wayfinder:task
labels.description: Execution authorized in the Effra Wayfinder map

body:
<!-- effra-wayfinder-id: jsx-notation -->
<!-- effra-wayfinder-source-sha256: 50498c3a8596408db4e63cfbae6cabc5e2e1ffeddfb58ffdb128eef367ef9e9e -->
<!-- effra-wayfinder-source-commit: 4627f414414cc964840b53894b7161482687de69 -->

Implement the accepted Option B notation only after the ordinary view library and interop contracts are ready. A user-defined pragma selects the checked ordinary lowering semantics; the exact pragma spelling remains a design input. JSX is queued syntax sugar, not a new effect, type, ownership or reactive runtime model, and the compiler does not hard-code React/Solid adapters or a mandatory view-node architecture. Effect execution/runtime selection is likewise userland-selected through a lawful checked implementation rather than implicit execution.

## Acceptance

- Parse the finite element/fragment/attribute/quoted-text forms and, for a declared user pragma, desugar each accepted form one-to-one to the pragma's ordinary checked calls. This one-to-one notation exception adds no hidden provider selection, host element, event tracking, subscription or cleanup behavior, and does not require `View.Node`/`Client.Element` or any framework adapter API.
- Type the user-defined factory, module and fragment choices as ordinary declarations, with explicit accessor/delay calls where needed; privileged framework names and hidden evaluation semantics are rejected. Two unrelated same-target pragma programs must compile without compiler edits, and a selected runtime must expose its actual JS representation and ABI honestly.
- Preserve labelled arguments, source spans, formatter output, LSP hover/definition/completion and visible desugaring. Diagnostics and effect/service/ownership rows must equal the explicit call form.
- Cover typed URL/style/script attributes, required attributes, fragments, prop punning, ordinary `if`/`match` children and negative controls for unsupported spreads, dynamic names, invalid tags, effect values used as nodes and unsafe raw content. Preserve explicit types, effect/service/failure rows and ownership through lowering; no implicit Effect execution is admitted.
- Run the same accepted programs through Go/JS and the selected provider/runtime interop. React, Solid 2 and solid-yield corpus rows validate pragma/runtime interop rather than bespoke compiler adapters. Record parse/emission receipts and independent review; design snippets alone remain unverified. The durable JSX pragma and target-qualified view record (public source sync pending: `docs/research/jsx-pragmas-and-runtime-selection.md`) owns the finite notation, source comparisons and rejected alternatives; selected runtime laws and evidence categories come from the lawful runtime contract (public source sync pending: `docs/research/lawful-runtime-contract.md`).

The notation does not imply hydration, streaming, framework parity or current compiler support. Client mount ownership remains the separate VW4 lifetime bridge.

Prior art: TypeScript's per-file [`@jsx` factory](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/jsxFactory.html) and [`jsxImportSource`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/jsxImportSource.html), plus Babel's [`transform-react-jsx` factory/fragment pragmas](https://babeljs.io/docs/babel-plugin-transform-react-jsx), show provider selection without fixing Effra's pragma spelling or semantics. They are source inputs, not current Effra support.

title: Generalized run sequencing and checked userland binding

repository.name: effra
repository.description: An experimental server language with explicit effect contracts, owned lifetimes, native Go executables and a JavaScript/Effect target.

body:
<!-- effra-wayfinder-id: run-binding -->

## Question

Can existing `run` become checked userland binding for other effectful and pure computation families, while preserving explicit failure/service contracts, owned lifetimes, Go-like readability and zero-cost lowering opportunities?

Owner input, 2026-10-08: explore monadic binding supporting other effectful or non-effectful computations. This is an investigation, not accepted syntax or implementation.

## Investigation

- Compare ordinary typed `flatMap` calls with a minimal sequencing rule. Follow construct admission: syntax/checker machinery needs a concrete invariant ordinary libraries cannot enforce, or an explicit admitted notation exception.
- Compare explicit lexical selection with coherent nominal-family selection; diagnose ambiguity and import-dependent rebinding. Keep binding-family selection separate from effect-runtime provider selection.
- Use pure Option/Result domain code and an owned service/resource Effect workflow. Preserve lazy Effect construction, public failure/service rows, current owner, cancellation and completed cleanup. Pure functions cannot secretly execute I/O.
- The rest of a block is the continuation. Preserve short-circuit behavior, evaluation order, nested returned data and explicit family adaptation. Multi-use or retained continuations must not duplicate or escape owned resources.
- Require a third user-authored family without compiler edits, shared semantic-model/desugaring inspection, two-target runnable comparisons and causal negative controls before admission. Monad method shape/laws alone do not establish cancellation, cleanup or foreign honesty.
- Record compile/retention costs and static direct-lowering candidates; comparative performance measurements remain last.

## Primary mechanisms

[Haskell do translation](https://www.haskell.org/onlinereport/haskell2010/haskellch3.html#x8-470003.14), [GHC qualified do](https://downloads.haskell.org/ghc/9.14.1/docs/users_guide/exts/qualified_do.html), [F# computation expressions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/fsharp/language-reference/computation-expressions), and [Scala comprehensions](https://docs.scala-lang.org/tour/for-comprehensions.html) supply mechanisms and counterexamples to compare. Pinned [Effect flatMap/gen](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/460272d30457f4697d8b8c52cad41caccbcace08/packages/effect/src/Effect.ts), [Option.gen](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/460272d30457f4697d8b8c52cad41caccbcace08/packages/effect/src/Option.ts) and [Result.gen](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/460272d30457f4697d8b8c52cad41caccbcace08/packages/effect/src/Result.ts) are separate comparisons. Locked installed4.0.1 and pinned upstream package4.0.1 have different source bytes; version names do not establish exact equivalence.

## Current limits

Accepted Effra currently permits run only for Effects in effect functions. Root ordinary-JS Option/Result controls passed, but no generalized Effra binding, Go comparison execution, lawful custom binder, performance improvement or syntax admission follows. Durable local research/source synchronization and independently reviewed prototype remain upcoming.
